newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds mostly flat in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds mostly flat in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were largely unchanged by late afternoon Friday, with yield spreads to Treasuries holding firm, market sources said.
Some traders said they were able to find tasty tidbits despite today's sparse economic calendar, which left many players hungry for action.
"We're seeing some buyers, so we've been nibbling at some stuff," said one head trader at a large New York firm.
"We've continued to dabble in some of these modest premiums," he said, referring to Ginnie Mae II 8.0 percent and 8.5 percent coupons.
"They represent a lot of oppurtunity for a high-yielding security with low volatility," he said, adding that "they don't have a ton of upside, but they don't have a ton of downside either."

One regional trader said she cited small institutional selling of mortgage type. But most of them have been disappointed because "they are not getting the levels that they think they should," she said.
By late afternoon, pass-throughs were mostly unchanged in all coupons.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 7.0 percent coupons were off 1/32 at 99-01/32, yielding 104 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were 1/32 lower as well, at 100-26/32 and 100-30/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 1/32 at 102-20/32 to yield 6.14 percent.
